account: Today has mostly followed my appointment book: market rounds, lunch at home, town accounts, tea with neighbour, and a return to the office. I feel something may be happening without me, but I have not established any secret gathering or unusual activity. The only suggestive detail is neighbour's mention of bakery lights. Neighbour said the baker called them 'everyday cheer'; I have not personally seen unusual lighting or learned when it occurs. The baker had thirty-two fresh loaves stocked and asked whether town gatherings might need bread. Townsfolk reported seeing the baker carrying wheat. Those details could all be ordinary bakery business, rather than preparations for an event. Neighbour said they had attended no neighbourhood gatherings and had seen no definite dock changes. The secretary confirmed my tea and maintained the appointment book; I have seen no evidence that either is concealing anything. Our accounts review was inconclusive because neither the secretary nor I located account records. The treasury contains 128 emeralds, but no records, and the secretary reported no unusual funding requests or expenses brought to their attention. That is an administrative gap, not proof of missing funds. I am back in the office; the appointments chest still holds two books. My best current assessment is that the bakery lights warrant a straightforward inquiry, but I cannot yet say that anything unusual is being organized, who would be involved, or what its purpose would be.
